editorial.publisher_title: David Choe Asks For a Billon Dollars
editorial.summary: A 2:35 derivative excerpt from Joe Rogan Experience #1965 in which the primary storyteller frames billionaire status as an attainable video-game goal after claiming hundreds of millions, distinguishes money from the lives of wealthy acquaintances, and argues that scarcity and social value turn money from a thing into the thing. He recounts asking an unnamed friend with hundreds of billions for one billion dollars, promising instinctive and maximally irresponsible use to change the planet, then recognizes money as power, rejects the responsibility, reports the friend’s no and says thank you. All ideas, masks, repetition and the refusal remain. Wealth, relationships, private dialogue and intentions stay self-report; the archive establishes no balance sheet, plan, offer, gift, investment, charitable commitment, impact or private billionaire identity. One damaged phrase remains unclear and zero line-level voices are named.
